gauges.name: Wisconsin River at Rothschild
gauges.description: Primary gauge for the Wausau metro area

tips.Walleye: Jigs tipped with minnows near current breaks and dam tailwaters. Best at dawn/dusk. Try 1/4 oz jig heads bounced along sandy bottoms.
tips.Smallmouth Bass: Crankbaits and tube jigs around rocky shorelines and bridge pilings. Topwater action in summer evenings.
tips.Musky: Large bucktails and jerkbaits along weed edges and deep structure. Fall is prime — focus on figure-8s at the boat.
tips.Channel Catfish: Cut bait or stink bait on the bottom near deeper holes. Night fishing in summer is most productive.
tips.Sturgeon: Catch-and-release only. Observe from shore during the spring spawning run — a spectacular sight near Rothschild dam.

season_notes: Walleye/Sauger open first Sat in May
Catch-and-release bass season Mar–Jun

gauges.description: Designated trout stream north of Wausau near Merrill

tips.Brook Trout: Small spinners (#0–#2 Mepps) or live worms in the upper reaches. Wade upstream quietly — brookies hold in cold, shaded pools and undercut banks.

gauges.name: Wolf River near Shawano
gauges.description: Lower Wolf at Shawano — the basin's flood-forecast point

tips.Walleye: Winnebago-system walleye push upriver to the Shawano dam in April — but the dam-to-County-M reach is a posted no-fishing refuge Apr 1–May 1. Drift jig-and-minnow along current seams downstream of the County M bridge until it reopens.
tips.White Bass: The famous run follows the walleye — May, classically peaking around Mother's Day. Small white jigs or inline spinners below the dam and off the Sturgeon Park pier.
tips.Smallmouth Bass: DNR-designated smallmouth water through town — float it in summer, working tubes and topwater around boulders and wood.
tips.Channel Catfish: Summer nights on cut bait or crawlers in the deeper holes below town; the river below the dam is open year-round for most species.
tips.Northern Pike: Work spoons and large minnows along the weedy margins of the millpond above the dam in spring and fall.

regulations.rule: Winnebago-system rules below the dam — 3 daily with new-for-2026 slot protection; check DNR for your reach
Closed to fishing on the river — the spring spawning run at the dam is watch-only
No fishing from the dam down to the Cty M bridge, Apr 1 until the Friday before the general opener (spring refuge)
14" min, 5 daily (special smallmouth rules on some stretches — check DNR)

season_notes: Lake sturgeon spawn below the Shawano dam in the second half of April — thousands come to watch at Sturgeon Park. Look, don't cast.
Spring walleye run late March–April; white bass peak mid-May; catfish take the deep holes June–August

gauges.name: North Fork Yellow River near Perkinstown
gauges.description: Chequamegon country stream in Taylor County

tips.Largemouth Bass: The nearby Chequamegon Waters Flowage is largemouth-first water — work weedlines and wild-rice bay edges with soft plastics or spinnerbaits.
tips.Northern Pike: Pike are the flowage's top predator (DNR surveys found no musky) — larger baits along weed edges, and the bite holds through the ice season.
tips.Panfish: Bluegill and crappie are the flowage's bread and butter — shallow wood early in the season, weed edges in summer.
tips.Walleye: DNR calls walleye here a rare bonus fish — the few caught tend to be large.

regulations.rule: 25 daily in total, no size limit (Chequamegon Waters Flowage)

season_notes: The gauge stream itself is not DNR-classified trout water — the local fishery is Chequamegon Waters Flowage (Miller Dam), ~8 miles southwest
Ice fishing is popular on the flowage; an aeration system runs Jan–March near the Yellow River inlet

gauges.name: Wisconsin River at Rainbow Lake near Lake Tomahawk
gauges.description: Headwaters gauge at Rainbow Reservoir — the top of the system

tips.Walleye: May is the peak month by DNR creel data — work sand flats and drop-offs early; most keepers run 15–17 inches.
tips.Musky: Dark-stained water warms early, making Rainbow a strong early-season pick — and with a special 50-inch minimum it fishes as trophy catch-and-release water.
tips.Smallmouth Bass: July is the busiest smallmouth month here; DNR netting found most adults over 14 inches. Catch-and-release only until June 19.
tips.Northern Pike: Pike action holds through the ice — January is the peak month. Tip-ups with large shiners over weed flats.
tips.Panfish: Crappie are the most-sought panfish and genuinely quality-sized (11-inch average in the last creel survey) — wood and creek arms after ice-out.

regulations.rule: 50" min on Rainbow Flowage (special — statewide is 40"), 1 daily
Catch-and-release until June 19, then 14" min, 5 daily
25 daily in total, no size limit

season_notes: WVIC storage reservoir: drawn down to minimum pool by late March, then refilled with snowmelt — expect low water and mudflats in early spring
Fishable ice typically forms mid-December; winter creel shows strong pike, perch, and walleye effort

upcoming_events.name: Inland Trout Season Closes
upcoming_events.description: Last day for inland trout on streams, springs, and spring ponds. The Prairie, Little Plover, Tomorrow, and Rib tributaries all close until the early catch-and-release period in January.

upcoming_events.name: Early Catch-and-Release Trout Opens
upcoming_events.description: Winter catch-and-release trout season opens on inland streams (artificials only). Runs until the regular season opener in April.

upcoming_events.name: Free Fishing Weekend (Winter)
upcoming_events.description: Jan. 16–17. No license or stamps required for residents or nonresidents — a great weekend to try ice fishing. All bag/size limits still apply.

upcoming_events.name: General Inland Game Fish Season Closes
upcoming_events.description: Walleye, northern pike, and most inland game fish seasons close on inland waters until the first Saturday in May.
